chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Abu al-Abbas Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Dahqan from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, the seller of al-Sabiri, from Aban, from Sabbah ibn Sayabat, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

I went with the letter of Abd al-Salam ibn Nueym and Sadir, and the letters of not just one person, to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), when the Black One appeared, before the sons of al-Abbas appear, saying: 'We have estimated that this Command will return to you, so what do you see?' He said, so he struck the letters on the ground, then said: 'Uff! Uff! I am not an Imam for these ones. Do they not know that he is the one who kills al-Sufyani?'

key_terms.أُفٍّ: An expression of dismissal or contempt
key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيَّ: Al-Sufyani, a key eschatological figure in Shia tradition
key_terms.الْمُسَوِّدَةُ: The Black One, a title for the Caliph al-Mansur or the Abbasid movement
key_terms.وُلْدُ الْعَبَّاسِ: The sons of Abbas, referring to the Abbasid Caliphs

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the expectation of the Imams taking political rule upon the appearance of al-Musawwadah?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the distinction between the political expectations of the early Abbasid supporters and the spiritual authority of the Imams, emphasizing that the Imam's role is defined by the ultimate victory over the Sufyani rather than immediate temporal rule. The act of striking the letters signifies the rejection of their premature claim to leadership, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology where the Mahdi's rise is preceded by the chaos of the Sufyani. This narrative underscores the patience required from the faithful as they await the divinely appointed time for the establishment of justice.
